label: defeated opponent
definition: X defeated opposing competitor Y in at least one competitive contest.
scope_notes: Preserves winner-to-opponent scope. Beat, defeat and victory over qualify. Playing/facing, standings, losing, communication and professional affiliation alone do not. A historical win remains support when other rows describe losses. The dictionary strongly mixes contest outcomes with directed communication; beat/defeat are its two most frequent paths. The chosen contest predicate is not uniquely compelled by this mixed cluster.

facts.reason: Mr. Clinton submits/sends to, persuades and works with Congress; these are communication/cooperation, not a competitive defeat.
Mr. Jordan tells and telephones Ms. Lewinsky; no defeat is expressed.
Gephardt tells House and has speaker/task-force associations; no defeat is expressed.
Bensonhurst and Brooklyn occur in a racial/location dependency path, not a contest.
Bush or the Bush administration asks and sends to Congress; no competitive defeat is expressed.
